subject: Discovery recap & model-fit recommendations for Halcyon — schema retries & next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@halcyonhealth.ai>, Tom Wilkes <tom.wilkes@halcyonhealth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T15:08:00-05:00
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed evaluation axis for Halcyon

Hi Asha / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment: 

Why you called: Halcyon wants an inference path for automated note summarization and structured extraction (claim type, care setting, ICD-like tags). Key constraints you called out:
- P95 latency target: ~350ms per request at expected 150 qps (burst to 350)
- Sensitive PHI detection required; want KMS/HSM integration and redaction options
- Output must be structured JSON with strict schema validation and a retry strategy for schema violations

Recommended initial evaluation plan (lightweight):
1) Models to bench (we'll run a focused eval suite):
   - Redwood-Instruct-7B (quantized int8 profile) — low latency baseline
   - Llama3-13B-QLoRA (13B) — balance accuracy vs cost
   - OrcaLite-1.0 (smaller context) — check structured-extraction recall
2) Tests we will run: exact-match field extraction, schema validation rate (JSON schema pass %), hallucination spot checks on 500 representative notes, and latency p95 under batching profiles
3) Tool/function-calling checks: exercise function signatures for (create_claim_record/json), (redact_pii/text) — verify type enforcement and retry paths on schema failures
4) Retry strategy we suggest: 2 automatic retry attempts with (a) relax strict-mode to best-effort JSON then (b) structured fallback that returns a minimal validated envelope + confidence tags. We'll measure how often fallback is needed and whether it reduces downstream errors.

What we need from you to kick off:
- A 300–500 sample of representative notes (de-identified or with an NDA) — prefer CSV/JSON latency-friendly format
- Clarify acceptable fallback envelope fields (what can be empty/omitted)
- Any existing JSON schema you require for the final payload (we can adapt to your schema if you share it)

I've attached a skeleton prompt set template (halcyon-prompt-set-v1.csv) and our initial model recommendations & benchmark plan (redwood-model-recs-and-benchmarks-20261109.pdf).

Next steps: if you can share a sample and confirm a 2–3 hour testing window next week (we can run the initial bench in that period), we'll schedule a follow-up to review metric outputs and pick a model/quantization profile to pilot.

Attachment: halcyon-prompt-set-v1.csv (CSV)
Attachment: redwood-model-recs-and-benchmarks-20261109.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — look forward to it.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@halcyonhealth.ai>

Date: 2026-11-09T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed evaluation axis for Halcyon

Connor — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side before we send samples: 

1) Latency/SLO: the 350ms p95 is for single-note requests with no heavy pre/post-processing. We expect spikes during batch ingest; can Redwood simulate tail-latency under our burst profile?
2) PHI handling: we'll need to see how KMS/HSM integrates with your private deployment option. For the pilot we can de-id, but long term we need to validate key mgmt and audit logs.
3) Schema/fallback: our product team says certain fields are mandatory (claim_id, patient_id, primary_diagnosis). Fallback envelope should include claim_id and a flagged boolean "needs_manual_review" if structured extraction fails.

We can share a de-identified 400-note CSV (E2E format) — I can have that to you by EOD tomorrow under our standard NDA. We'd also like you to include a small test for function-calling correctness (i.e., will the model produce exactly the function name and argument types per signature) — that's critical for our downstream ingest.

Tom and I are free for a short sync on Wednesday 11/11 (10–11am PT) if you want to walk through the sample format live.

Thanks,
Asha
Head of Applied ML | Halcyon Health
asha.mehta@halcyonhealth.ai

Connor / Karthik — quick internal notes before we run the bench: 

- Karthik: can you prioritize a run that measures JSON schema pass rate as a first-class metric (we need per-field validation stats, not just whole-document pass) and include token-level timing to identify hot spans causing tail latency. Use our standard eval harness and flag any model where schema pass < 95% on the 400-sample set.
- For function calling, include 3 variants per signature: correct args order, extra unexpected arg, and missing optional arg — this will exercise decoder behavior and our retry policy.
- Retry policy: implement 2 back-to-back retries with slightly relaxed schema enforcement: attempt1 strict JSON schema; attempt2 allow relaxed typing (coerce num strings); attempt3 fallback envelope (claim_id + needs_manual_review=true). Track how many responses reach fallback.
- Security: confirm that logs redact PII by default and that audit events include KMS key id and ephemeral key usage (we'll ask security to validate once we have a pilot environment).

I'll draft the exact eval job spec and share in Drive (will add to the related_links). ETA for internal bench run: 48 hours after receiving the sample. If that timeline holds, we can present results in the Wed 11/11 sync.

Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
